comparator.name: Biology
comparator.sourceNotes: Current2026programme controls: compulsory105+backgroundchoice3+restrictedRO2six+restrictedRO3twelve+thesis24=150,plusopen30. No formal major is specified. MathematicsA entry and first-listed laboratory RO2 are illustrative neutral choices; RO3 remains an aggregate pending supervising-chair preparation requirements. Programme requires two chair-preparing RO3 courses; module assumed-knowledge wording of at leastone does not waive that rule. Mandatory registration deadline and zero-credit safety/portfolio preserved. Numeric180doesnotcertifycompletepathway.
components: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
The Philosophy and Ethics of Biology
Nine-credit organismal course. The zero-credit Biology Skills Portfolio and general, laboratory and fieldwork safety requirements are separate obligations.
Six-credit compulsory Advanced Statistics remains included. The thesis module’s assumed-knowledge alternative of Ecological Methods does not remove this programme requirement.
Example for a student entering with VWO Mathematics A: Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead.

Illustrative first-listed restricted option: Practical from Gene to Protein, for a cellular, plant or animal biology direction. Other directions use Molecular and Evolutionary Ecology. The final specialisation and thesis preparation remain unverified.

Required 24-credit research project. Before starting, complete at least 102 prescribed credits including all first-year credits and pass the two restricted specialisation courses preparing for the supervising chair. Current chair-specific course allocation remains unverified. Registration at least one month before starting is mandatory; discuss a project about four months beforehand.
At least 12 credits must be chosen from the prescribed specialisation list. The final choices must prepare for the supervising thesis chair; this aggregate is not an instantiated course pair.
Thirty credits remain open for a minor, individual minor or elective courses.

alternatives.label: Biological sciences: cells, organisms & ecosystems
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule visibly spans molecular and cellular biology, physiology, organisms, evolution, ecology, biodiversity, environmental study, data and research, matching WUR’s cell-to-ecosystem breadth.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Biology programme spanning cellular and molecular life, genetics, physiology, organisms, evolution, ecology, biodiversity, laboratory and field methods, statistics.
progression: Current workbook offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass; first-yearPPD and six300-level minimum pass. Brain/behaviour precedes psycholinguistics, mathematics precedes dependent data/statistics, and life foundations precede all dependent biology. Independent advanced ecology retains the open curriculum’s actual formal rules.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & health biology
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, disease, immunity, neuroscience, laboratory work and data analysis form the visible spine.
alternatives.concept: Concentrates on cell biology, molecular mechanisms, genetics, biochemistry, physiology, microbiology, immunology, disease, neuroscience, laboratory research and biological data analysis.
progression: Current workbook offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass; first-yearPPD and six300-level minimum pass. Brain/behaviour precedes psycholinguistics, mathematics precedes dependent data/statistics, and life foundations precede all dependent biology. Independent advanced ecology retains the open curriculum’s actual formal rules.
alternatives.distinctness: Different priorities molecular/physiological and neurocognitive mechanisms with biological data analysis have material curricular consequences. Pairwise unique counts 6. Provisional only while external pathway unresolved.

alternatives.label: Ecology, evolution & conservation biology
alternatives.labelReason: Ecology, evolution, biodiversity, conservation, field methods and environmental systems dominate the schedule, with biology foundations retained.
alternatives.concept: Concentrates on biodiversity, ecology, evolution, conservation, organisms, climate, soils, farming, environmental observation and field-based research across changing ecosystems.
progression: Current workbook offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass; first-yearPPD and six300-level minimum pass. Brain/behaviour precedes psycholinguistics, mathematics precedes dependent data/statistics, and life foundations precede all dependent biology. Independent advanced ecology retains the open curriculum’s actual formal rules.
alternatives.distinctness: Different priorities biodiversity, ecosystems, conservation and environmental chemical processes with genetic/physiological foundations have material curricular consequences. Pairwise unique counts 4,10. Provisional only while external pathway unresolved.

core: Cellular, genetic, physiological and organismal biology
Ecology, evolution, biodiversity and organism-environment relationships
Mathematics, statistics, programming and biological data/models
Laboratory and field biological investigation, chemistry and physics
adjacent: Molecular and health applications of biological knowledge
Neural and behavioural mechanisms in organisms
questions: How do biological processes interact across scales?
How can biology improve health and nature?

trace: Importing, cleaning, joining and visualising tabular/spatial data in R and a data research project directly support biological data analysis.
Introduces predictive modelling and machine-learning workflows for complex data.
Adds image analysis relevant to microscopy, anatomy and biological pattern recognition.
Provides neural-network methods for modelling complex biological and biomedical data.
Builds programming foundations useful for biological data analysis and bioinformatics.
Provides mathematical techniques needed for quantitative and computational biological work.
Adds probability, distributions, sampling, estimation and simulation for biological inference.
Surveys the tree of life, microorganisms, plants, animals and methods for investigating biodiversity.
Examines extinction, human impacts and scientific and policy responses in conservation biology.
Studies evolutionary mechanisms from genes to populations and their application across biology.
Covers ecological processes from organisms to ecosystems and introduces ecological modelling.
Develops marine ecology across estuaries, coasts and coral reefs and assesses human impacts.
Studies organisms, food systems, environmental impacts and ecological innovations in farming.
Connects organisms and ecosystems to soil processes, water and environmental conditions.
Description-supported biosphere-water-rock-atmosphere interactions, system modelling, isotope/proxy analysis and greenhouse-gas fieldwork complement ecosystem-process investigation.
Connects biological systems to nutrient cycles and chemical processes in the environment.
Nutrient cycles, ocean acidification, dynamic environmental models and laboratory biopolymer testing provide a specific environmental chemistry/physics complement to ecosystem biology.
Greenhouse feedbacks, tipping points, ocean acidification and ecosystem/agricultural impacts support biological responses to environmental change; societal response content is complementary.
Develops structure–function reasoning through human anatomy, imaging and anatomical variation.
Applies molecular, cellular and physiological regulation to pharmacology and toxic effects.
Studies microbes, host–pathogen interaction, innate and adaptive immunity and immunopathology.
Relates embryology, anatomy and physiology to mechanisms of disease across organ systems.
Provides comparative neurobiology, animal behaviour, microscopy, anatomy and experimental ethics.
Examines sensory and motor systems connecting neural mechanisms to perception and action.
Extends biological and cognitive analysis to advanced brain functions.

Description-supported evolution of language and animal communication, neural speech mechanisms and hands-on experimental approaches provide a bounded biological cognition contribution; no generic software neural-network equivalence.
Introduces cellular function, genetics, physiology, microorganisms and experimental biological reasoning.

Neural signalling, brain development, learning and combined behavioural/imaging/electrophysiological approaches complement the study of animal behaviour and neurobiology; not a replacement for organismal zoology.
Develops molecular-cell biology, genomes, gene expression, signalling, division, tissues and current research methods.
Examines molecules, cells, tissues, organ systems, homeostasis and organismal physiology.
Covers biomolecules, metabolism, signalling and biochemical foundations of biotechnology and disease.
Provides molecular and microbiological laboratory work, including proteins, PCR, electrophoresis and bioinformatics.
Advances molecular genetics, mutation, inheritance, pathology, testing and treatment.

notes.text: The UCR programmes provide related biological study, but do not reproduce all plant and animal specialisms, chemical and physical laboratory sequences or the required24-credit thesis. Optional UCR research is additional to each180-credit schedule.
